Rashi on Gittin 56a:10:1.english: Biryonei [ruffians] - Worthless and reckless men [eager] for war:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:10:2.english: The Sages said to them - to those zealots:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:10:3.english: The matter will not succeed - [meaning] to be victorious:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:10:5.hebrew: קלינהו להנך אמברי - לאוצרות התבואה ועצים, כדי שילחמו:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:10:5.english: They burned those ambarei - [meaning] the storehouses of grain and wood, so that they would fight:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:12:2.english: And she died - due to her delicateness:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:1.hebrew: גרוגרות - מאותם שנשארו לרבי צדוק שמצץ את מימיה, ומצאתה היא ואכלת' לרעבונה, ומריח החולי של רבי צדוק שנכנס בגרוגרת, טעמה ומתה באסטניסו':
Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:1.english: Dried figs - [A fig] from those that were left over by Rabbi Tzadok, whose liquid he had sucked out; she found it and ate it in her hunger, and from the odor of Rabbi Tzadok's illness that had entered the dried fig, she tasted [it] and died from squeamishness:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:2.english: It was visible - in his throat:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:3.english: From the outside - because he was emaciated:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:4.english: When he would eat - when he finished his fasts and wanted to nourish himself:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:5.hebrew: הוו מייתי ליה גרוגרות - תאנים יבשין, מפני שלא היה יכול לבלוע דבר עבה, והיה מוצץ את מימיהן ומשליך הגרוגרות:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:13:5.english: They would bring him figs - dried figs, because he was unable to swallow anything solid, and he would suck out their liquid and throw away the figs:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:15:1.english: Abba Sikkara - That was his name:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:15:2.hebrew: שלח ליה - רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, "תא לגבאי בצנעא":
Rashi on Gittin 56a:15:2.english: He sent to him - Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai [sent to him], "Come to me in secret":

Rashi on Gittin 56a:15:3.english: He said to him - Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai [said this]:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:15:4.english: Until when will you do this - [Meaning,] that you do not allow [us] to make peace.

Rashi on Gittin 56a:15:5.english: Find a plan for me - [a way] that they will let me leave the city.

Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:1.hebrew: נקוט נפשך בקצירי - החזק עצמך כחולה, הוציא קול שאתה חולה:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:1.english: Hold yourself among the sick - Act as though you are sick, [and] spread word that you are sick:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:2.english: Let them inquire about you - as though you are dying.

Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:3.english: And bring something putrid - Something foul-smelling, such as a carcass:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:4.hebrew: ואגני גבך - והשכב במטתך עמך, שיאמרו מת הוא ומסריח כבר:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:4.english: And lay [it] beside you - And lay [it] down in your bed with you, so that they will say, "He is dead and already stinking":

Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:5.hebrew: וליעיילו בך תלמידך - יכנסו תחת רגלי מטתך לשאת, ולא יניחו אחרים לשאת, דאינון ידעין דחייא קליל ממיתה:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:16:5.english: And have your students enter - They shall enter under the legs of your bier to carry [you], and they shall not allow others to carry [you], for they know that a living [person] is lighter than a dead [person]:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:17:2.english: To pierce him - With spears, lest he is tricking [them].

Rashi on Gittin 56a:17:3.english: He said to them - Abba Sikkara:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:17:4.english: They will say - the Romans [will say] about you that they pierced even their teacher:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:17:5.english: To push him - Perhaps he would cry out:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:18:1.english: Because I am not a king - and you mocked me:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:1:1.hebrew: א"ל לא - שביקנא לך:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:1:1.english: He said to him: No - [I will not] let you [stay]:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:1:2.hebrew: א"ל - איהו קאמר "יהיבנא לך דמי פלגא סעודתך":
Rashi on Gittin 56a:1:2.english: He said to him - [Meaning,] he [Bar Kamtza] says, "I will give you the value of half of your feast":

Rashi on Gittin 56a:2:2.hebrew: קורבנא - קרבן להקריב על גבי המזבח, דקיימא לן: "איש איש", לרבות את עובדי כוכבים שנודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל (חולין דף יג:):
Rashi on Gittin 56a:2:2.english: An offering - A sacrifice to offer upon the altar, for we hold: "Any man" [is written] to include gentiles, that they may vow vowed offerings and freewill offerings like an Israelite (Chullin 13b):

Rashi on Gittin 56a:3:1.english: On the niv sefatayim - [This refers to] the upper lip:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:3:2.hebrew: לדידהו לא הוי מומא - להקריב לגבוה בבמה דידהו, אלא מחוסר אבר. דוקין — טיל"ה, כמו "הנוטה כדוק" (ישעיהו מ):
Rashi on Gittin 56a:3:2.english: According to them it is not a blemish - [with respect] to offering to the Most High on their altar; rather, [only] a missing limb [is considered a blemish]. Dukin [means] toile [Old French: a film or membrane], like "Who stretches out [the heavens] like a curtain (kedok)" (Isaiah 40):

Rashi on Gittin 56a:4:1.hebrew: יאמרו המטיל מום בקדשים יהרג - שיהו סבורין שבשביל שהטיל מום בקדשים ועבר על "מום לא יהיה בו" (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״א), נהרג:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:4:1.english: They will say, "One who makes a blemish on sacrificial [animals] is to be killed" - [That is,] they will think that because he made a blemish on sacrificial [animals] and transgressed [the verse], "there shall be no blemish in it" (Leviticus 22:21), he was put to death:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:5:1.hebrew: ענותנותו - סבלנותו, שסבל את זה ולא הרגו:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:5:1.english: His humility - His forbearance, [in] that he tolerated this [one] and did not kill him.

Rashi on Gittin 56a:6:1.english: He shot an arrow to the east - to perform divination when he was near Jerusalem:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:7:1.hebrew: ההוא ינוקא - "הוה מגמגם בלישניה", לא גרסינן:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:7:1.english: That child - [The phrase] "was stuttering in his speech" — we do not have this reading:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:7:2.english: By the hand of My people Israel - Through My people Israel:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:7:3.english: And to wipe his hands - To wipe his hands:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:8:1.hebrew: נקדה - נקבה, לשון "מקדרין בהרים" (עירובין דף נח.); "נקדה לו חמה" — זרחה בשבילו, במסכת תענית (דף כ.):
Rashi on Gittin 56a:8:1.english: Shined [nakdah] - [This means] "pierced," [similar to] the expression "piercing through mountains" (Eruvin 58a). "The sun shined [nakdah] on his behalf" [means] it shone for him, [as related] in Tractate Ta'anit (20a):

Rashi on Gittin 56a:8:2.english: His tzitzit - the tzitzit [ritual fringes] of his tallit:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:8:3.english: Dragged upon cushions and blankets - [meaning] that he would walk only upon fine wool [cloths]:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:8:4.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי - בן ציצית שמו, ולמה נקרא שמו "הכסת"? שהיתה כסתו — כסא שלו — מוטלת בין גדולי רומי, כשהי' הולך ברומי להקביל פני קיסר:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:8:4.english: And there are [those] who say - Ben Tzitzit was his name, and why was he called "HaKeset"? Because his keset — [meaning] his seat — was placed among the nobles of Rome when he would go to Rome to greet Caesar:

Rashi on Gittin 56a:9:1.hebrew: הוו להו - להנך תלתא עתירי חיטי ושערי וחמרא וציבי, למיזן כל בני העיר עשרים וחד שתא:
Rashi on Gittin 56a:9:1.english: They had - those three wealthy men [had] wheat, barley, wine, and wood, to sustain all the residents of the city [for] twenty-one years:

Tosafot on Gittin 56a:1:1.hebrew: עגלא תילתא - כמו "ושלישים על כולו" (שמות י״ד:ז׳), וכמו "עגלה משולשת ואיל משולש" (בראשית ט״ו:ט׳), פי': בריא וטוב. ויש מפרשים: שלישי לבטן. ולא יתכן, דאמרינן בפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף סה:) דהוו מברו להו עיגלא תלתא. ולא כמו שמפרש שגדל שליש, דהא בסוף פרק רבי אליעזר דמילה (שבת דף קלו.) אמר: עבד להו עגלא תילתא ביומא דשבעא — פירוש, יום שביעי ללידתו [וע"ע תוספות בכורות יט. ד"ה דהך שלא וכו']:
Tosafot on Gittin 56a:1:1.english: Egla tilta - Like [the verse] "and captains [shalishim] over all of them" (Exodus 14:7), and like "a threefold [meshuleshet] heifer and a threefold [meshulash] ram" (Genesis 15:9) — meaning: healthy and good. And some explain [it as]: the third [born] from the womb. But this is not plausible, for we say in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 65b) that they would create for themselves an egla tilta. And [it is] also not as [one] explains, that it had grown a third [of its full size]; for at the end of the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer deMilah (Shabbat 136a), it says: He made for them an egla tilta on the seventh day — meaning, the seventh day from its birth [and see further Tosafot on Bekhorot 19a, s.v. "de'hakh shelo," etc.]:
